title: Final Foundations Knowledge Assessment
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of final foundations knowledge assessment.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: A final knowledge assessment checks understanding across programming foundations rather than memorization of isolated terms. Learners should explain concepts, trace behavior, choose data structures, reason about functions and control flow, recognize risks, and interpret API communication scenarios. Assessment results identify topics that need review; they are not a substitute for building and explaining a project.
understand.whyItMatters: A comprehensive assessment helps learners identify strengths and gaps before progressing to more specialized programming courses.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
A final knowledge assessment checks understanding across programming foundations rather than memorization of isolated terms. Learners should explain concepts, trace behavior, choose data structures, reason about functions and control flow, recognize risks, and interpret API communication scenarios. Assessment results identify topics that need review; they are not a substitute for building and explaining a project.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

examples.title: Create topic coverage
examples.explanation: Coverage planning helps avoid over-testing one topic.

examples.title: Use varied question types
examples.explanation: Different question styles measure different kinds of understanding.

examples.title: Record an outcome
examples.explanation: A score can summarize performance but does not explain every learning gap.

examples.title: Identify review topics
examples.explanation: Missed topics can guide targeted review.

examples.title: Explain reasoning
examples.code:
const explanation='I selected this option because the boundary check rejects the invalid value';
console.log(explanation.length>0);
examples.explanation: Explaining why strengthens understanding beyond guessing.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Create a mini assessment with questions from conditions, loops, data, functions, collections, debugging, security, and APIs. Include at least one code-tracing question and one scenario-based question. Review incorrect answers afterward.
steps: Create a mini assessment with questions from conditions, loops, data, functions, collections, debugging, security, and APIs. Include at least one code-tracing question and one scenario-based question. Review incorrect answers afterward.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Complete a self-assessment covering foundations. For each topic, rate confidence, answer or solve a task, explain your reasoning, identify gaps, and create a targeted review plan. Do not treat a score alone as proof of mastery.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.

Complete a self-assessment covering foundations. For each topic, rate confidence, answer or solve a task, explain your reasoning, identify gaps, and create a targeted review plan. Do not treat a score alone as proof of mastery.
Include a short test plan and results.

hints: Mix recall, tracing, scenario, and debugging questions.
Cover all major modules rather than only recent topics.
Include explanation for the correct answer.
Use incorrect answers to plan revision.
Demonstrate concepts in a small project as well as a quiz.
